question: What is the primary purpose of a health care budget?

options.A: To eliminate all unexpected hospital expenses permanently
options.B: To calculate exact salaries for individual doctors and nurses
options.C: To plan and control financial resources for medical services
options.D: To set the retail prices of medications in the pharmacy

explanation: A health care budget serves as a financial plan to guide how money is spent on patient care services. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is financial resource management considered a key part of nursing practice?

options.A: Nurses are solely responsible for auditing hospital accounts
options.B: Nurse managers must directly purchase hospital real estate
options.C: Ensuring supplies do not run out is vital for safe patient care
options.D: Clinical care is completely separate from financial planning

explanation: Proper budgeting prevents critical shortages of daily medical supplies needed at the bedside. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h1)

question: What does equity in a healthcare budget mean?

options.A: Distributing health services fairly so vulnerable populations receive care
options.B: Giving every single department the exact same amount of cash
options.C: Allowing only wealthy patients to access specialized treatments
options.D: Ensuring the hospital makes a profit on every patient admitted

explanation: Budgetary equity focuses on fair distribution so that those in need, including vulnerable groups, can access care. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h2)

question: What does accountability mean for a nurse unit manager regarding finances?

options.A: Personally paying for any broken equipment on the ward
options.B: Deciding how much profit the entire hospital should make
options.C: Setting the tax rates that fund the local health facility
options.D: Being responsible for staying within the assigned departmental budget

explanation: Accountability means managers must answer for how funds are spent in their unit and keep expenses within limits. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which type of budget is used to purchase expensive, long-term equipment like a new MRI machine?
explanation: Capital budgets are specifically set aside for large, long-term investments and major equipment. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h3)

question: A nurse manager needs to buy daily supplies of syringes and gauze. Under which budget category do these routine expenses fall?
explanation: Routine, day-to-day operational costs like medical supplies and staff salaries are managed through the operating budget. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is zero-based budgeting?

options.A: Cutting all nursing salaries down to zero during a financial crisis
options.B: Simply adding five percent to whatever was spent last year
options.C: Requiring departments to justify all expenses from scratch every year
options.D: Operating the hospital with zero money until donations arrive

explanation: Zero-based budgeting forces managers to prove the value of every single cost rather than just copying the previous year. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the main drawback of traditional incremental budgeting?

options.A: It requires every single nurse to have a degree in accounting
options.B: It completely stops all purchases of new hospital equipment
options.C: It can carry forward wasteful spending from past years without question
options.D: It takes too much time to calculate compared to zero-based budgeting

explanation: Because incremental budgeting just adds to old totals, past inefficiencies often get repeated automatically. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h4)

question: What does cost containment mean in healthcare?

options.A: Firing all senior nurses to replace them with students
options.B: Closing down hospital wards to save money on electricity
options.C: Reducing expenses without harming the quality of patient care
options.D: Refusing to treat patients who cannot pay cash immediately

explanation: Cost containment is about finding smart ways to save money while keeping patient outcomes safe and high quality. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h5)

question: A hospital ward has very low patient admission numbers for the week. What is a smart cost-containment action the nurse manager can take?

options.A: Turn off the emergency generators to save on diesel fuel costs
options.B: Throw away all leftover medications to clear out the pharmacy
options.C: Adjust shift schedules to avoid paying unnecessary overtime wages
options.D: Refuse to admit any new patients until the following month

explanation: Matching staff levels to patient workload prevents unnecessary spending on overtime during quiet periods. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is an unfavorable budget variance?

options.A: When department managers refuse to write a new financial plan
options.B: When actual expenses exceed the planned budget amount
options.C: When the hospital makes more money than it originally expected
options.D: When staff members refuse to work overtime shifts

explanation: An unfavorable variance means the facility or unit spent more money than it was allocated. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why must nurse managers review monthly financial reports?

options.A: To catch and investigate budget variances before they become major deficits
options.B: To determine which nurses should be disciplined for making mistakes
options.C: To change the medical diagnoses written in patient clinical charts
options.D: To calculate the annual bonus for the hospital's chief executive officer

explanation: Monthly reviews allow managers to spot overspending early and take corrective action. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary way many Nigerian patients currently pay for healthcare services?
explanation: A large portion of healthcare financing in Nigeria relies on direct out-of-pocket payments by individuals. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical challenge faced in Nigerian healthcare budgeting?

options.A: Inflation driving up the cost of imported medical drugs
options.B: Delays in the official release of approved budget allocations
options.C: Instantaneous release of excess government funds every single week
options.D: Unpredictable revenue caused by low health insurance coverage

explanation: Delayed funding releases are a known challenge, so instantaneous weekly funding is incorrect. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h7)
